narr: Thunderstorms first developed along the sea breeze in the early afternoon hours on the southeast South Carolina coast. The thunderstorms then shifted inland along an outflow boundary and became nearly stationary across the Charleston Tri-County region. The thunderstorms repeatedly passed through an area from around Summerville and North Charleston. Extremely heavy rainfall occurred, producing flash flooding in this region. Thunderstorms also impacted the Walterboro area, producing damaging wind gusts.
ev: Dorchester County Emergency Management reported flash flooding at two locations near Highway 61, Bacon's Bridge Road, and Dorchester Road. Flood waters were entering a residence on West Walnut Circle and another residence on White Church Lane. A personal weather station located one street west of White Church Lane measured 4.90 inches of rain between 5:04 pm EST and 11:39 pm EST. A personal weather station located just west of West Walnut Circle measured 5.31 inches of rain between 4:59 pm EST and 10:19 pm EST.

Charleston County dispatch reported water entering bottom floor apartments on North Kenwood Drive. Nearby CoCoRaHS observers reported that 3.5-5 inches of rain fell in this area, with most of that rainfall occurring in a 2-3 hour period of time.
